text:
Sara: FYI Im seeing a steady memory/residency climb on the KV cache for very long sessions (>10k tokens) in the canary pool. Not a spikemore of a slow drift over the session.
Alex: can you share the time-series and a heap profile? curious if it's allocator fragmentation or genuine retention.
Sara: pasted key logs and the prom queries I used. snapshot of logs:
```
[2026-03-18T14:02:00Z] kv_cache.residency.p95=0.83
[2026-03-18T14:12:00Z] kv_cache.residency.p95=0.88
[2026-03-18T14:12:05Z] kv_evictions.total=14321 kv_evictions.success=14000
[2026-03-18T14:12:05Z] kv_slab.free_bytes=1209856 kv_page_fragments=195432
```
Prom queries I ran:
```
kv_cache.residency_percentile{quantile="0.95"}
rate(kv_cache.evictions_total[5m])
kv_cache.reuse_hitrate{model!=""}
```
Mike: interesting that evictions >0 but residency still rises. two quick possibilities:
- allocator fragmentation: free bytes exist but not in the right chunk sizes so effective capacity is lower
- eviction attribution is coarse (no shard/model tag) so we're not seeing hot-spot evictions
Jen: agree. also consider long-tail key variety: if a session keeps generating new unique keys (prefixes) reuse will naturally drop and residency climbs because the cache fills with one-off entries.
Sara: attached two sanitized heap dumps and a perf trace (s3://redwood-debug/kv-dumps/1767123456/). heap diffs show a lot of small allocations pinned to specific slabs.
Mike: ran a local stress with 15k token sessions; saw kv_fragmentation_ratio jump 0.10 -> 0.52. will land a metric to emit per-slab occupancy + eviction_age histogram. snippet:
```
metrics.emit("kv_slab.occupancy", ["slab_id", slab.id], value=occupied_bytes / slab.size)
metrics.histogram("kv_eviction.age_seconds", ["shard", shard.id], value=time_since_last_use)
```
Alex: nice. please add model and pool tags on eviction counters so we can relate to heavy models (llama-70b spawns lots of small prefixes).
Jen: dashboard ideas:
- p50/p90/p95 residency by model+pool
- evictions per_shard + success/fail rate
- slab occupancy heatmap (slab_id vs time)
- fragmentation ratio (usable_bytes / free_bytes)
- reuse_hitrate sliced by session-length buckets (0-1k,1k-5k,5k-20k,20k+)
Sara: propose alert: if p95_residency increases >20 percentage points over 30m AND rate(evictions[5m]) > 2x baseline -> page ops and eng-runtime.
ops-bot: New alert created KV-RESIDENCY-DRIFT-176712 (p95_delta>0.2 over 30m && rate(kv_cache.evictions_total[5m]) > 2*avg_over_time(kv_cache.evictions_total[1h])). Notify: #eng-runtime.
Mike: i'll send the metric patch today and wire up Grafana panels. can someone pair on heap diff analysis?
Alex: I can after standup. i'll also add per-model tags to eviction counters in the same PR.
Jen: i'll draft a short triage playbook (checks: p95 residency, evictions by shard, slab occupancy, fragmentation ratio, reuse_hitrate) and add links to the new panels.
Sara: TL;DR: sustained residency climb on very long contexts, evictions present but not explanatory. likely fragmentation + per-slab occupancy mismatch + long-tail unique keys. Action owners: Mike (metrics + grafana), Alex (eviction tagging + heap diffs), Jen (dashboard + playbook), Sara (sample sessions + repro data). ops-bot alert in place.
Alex: ack :thumbsup:
Mike: on it :wrench:
Jen: will produce playbook draft by EOD :spiral_note_pad:
